name: scenario_Effects_teardown_under_a_running_pipeline
description: Removing modules while the lights are still rendering. A module that is taken away mid-frame must leave the pipeline running on whatever it can still reach, rather than following a pointer to something that is gone.

fixture.name: layouts
fixture.description: Where the lights are, which the layer reads its coordinates from.

fixture.name: grid
fixture.description: A 16x16 panel: small enough to run anywhere, and every light is one the teardown could strand.

fixture.name: layer
fixture.description: One layer over those layouts, which owns the buffer every check below reads.

fixture.name: effect
fixture.description: An effect that paints from the first frame, so the pipeline is genuinely running before anything is removed.

fixture.name: drivers
fixture.description: The drivers container, wired to the effects whose buffer it reads.

fixture.name: preview
fixture.description: The preview is a driver like any other, and the one every target has.

fixture.name: services
fixture.description: The container a producer lives under, mirroring what boot wires.

steps.name: measure-baseline
steps.description: The pipeline rendering on its own, which every later measurement is read against.

steps.name: add-producer
steps.description: An audio producer: it acquires a source and publishes a frame every other audio module reads.

steps.name: add-consumer
steps.description: And a consumer of it, under the same layer the rainbow renders into, so two effects composite while a producer feeds one of them.

steps.name: measure-wired
steps.description: Producer and consumer both live. The difference against the baseline is what the pair costs.

steps.name: remove-the-producer-first
steps.description: THE CASE THIS EXISTS FOR. The microphone goes while the consumer is still rendering: it must fall back to the service's static silence rather than reading through a pointer to a module that has been destroyed.

steps.name: measure-orphaned-consumer
steps.description: The consumer outlived its producer and the lights are still on. A dangling read shows up here as a crash rather than a number.

steps.name: the-consumer-still-renders
steps.description: Its producer is gone, so it reads the service's static silence. Reporting its own control at all is what says the module is alive rather than dangling.

steps.name: remove-the-orphan
steps.description: And the consumer itself, which is the ordinary half: a module removed with nothing depending on it.

steps.name: measure-back-to-baseline
steps.description: Both gone. The cost should return to the baseline, since what was added has been fully released rather than merely unhooked.

steps.name: remove-the-rendering-effect
steps.description: The last effect under the layer, so the layer is left with a buffer and nothing to paint into it. An empty layer is a state the pipeline has to hold rather than a reason to stop.

steps.name: measure-empty-layer
steps.description: A layer with no effect at all: the floor, and proof the teardown reached it without taking the buffer with it.

steps.name: the-grid-outlived-its-effects
steps.description: Every effect is gone and the layout still reports the size it was built with: the teardown took the effects and left the pipeline standing.

steps.name: add-an-effect-back
steps.description: And one back in the same slot, because a pipeline that tears down cleanly but cannot be rebuilt is only half working.

steps.name: measure-rebuilt
steps.description: Rendering again after a full teardown and rebuild, which is what leaves the buffer checks below something to assert.

steps.name: the-rebuilt-effect-is-there
steps.description: And the new effect answers, which is what makes the rebuild a rebuild rather than an empty slot.

steps.name: add-a-second-driver
steps.description: A driver beside the preview, so the container holds one module a user added and one that is apparatus.

steps.name: clear-the-drivers
steps.description: Clear the container rather than naming what to remove, which is how a scenario prepares its own canvas on a device whose tree it did not build. The rule it has to honour is that apparatus stays: a preview, a board or an Improv submodule is not content.

steps.name: the-apparatus-survived-the-clear
steps.description: THE RULE THIS EXISTS FOR. The preview still answers after a clear that took the driver beside it, which is what says clear_children skipped the non-editable submodule rather than emptying the container wholesale.

steps.name: measure-after-the-clear
steps.description: Still rendering into the preview with the added driver gone.
